# dsh-persona-slot
Per-session persona slot for DeepSeek Harness. Every session holds **exactly one** persona — writing
a new one replaces the old instead of layering — and one global persona covers every session that h
as no persona of its own. Persona length is unbounded. Edit either from the conversation with `/pers
ona`, or from the panel under **Plugins → Installed**.
中文说明
## Why this exists
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona` gives one persona to a whole preset. That is the right tool when every se
ssion of a preset should be the same character. It cannot answer the other two questions:
- *This* session should be a cat, and that one should be a lawyer — at the same time, in the same wi

ndow.
- The persona should be changeable while the conversation is already running.
This plugin answers both. It resolves a persona per session from three tiers and applies it through
one agent-scoped prompt hook, so two sessions never see each other's choice and a change takes effec
t on the next model step.
## One persona per session
That is a guarantee, not a convention:
- A session's store record is single-valued; `set` replaces, so a third write overwrites the second

and never concatenates.
- Resolution returns at the first tier that holds a record, so an exact-sess

ion persona and the global persona never both reach one prompt.
- `one persona per session` and `a s
ession never resolves two personas at once` pin both rules in the unit suite.
## Resolution order
The first tier that holds a record wins.
| Order | Tier | Where it lives |

| 1 | exact session id | `config.sessions["<id>"]` or the runtime store |
| 2 | wildcard `"*"` | `co

nfig.sessions["*"]` or the runtime store |
| 3 | global | `config.global` or the runtime store |
A record is either text — used as the persona — or an explicit blank, which **mutes** that tier. Wit
h `blankOverrides: true` (the default) a blank stops the lookup, so a session can silence itself wit
hout deleting the deployment default. With `blankOverrides: false` a blank falls through to the next
eleting the deployment default. With `blankOverrides: false` a blank falls through to the next tier.

## Configure
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `global` | `""` | Persona every session inherits |
| `sessions` | `{}` | Per-session personas; `"*

"` is the wildcard tier |
| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch; `false` injects nothing and keeps st

ored text |
| `mode` | `append` | `append` adds a section, `replace` rewrites the deployment persona

|
| `prefix` | `""` | Text written above the persona |
| `suffix` | `""` | Text written below the p

ersona |
| `blankOverrides` | `true` | Whether a blank record mutes its tier instead of falling thro

ugh |
| `includeSubagents` | `true` | Whether subagent sessions also resolve a persona |
`mode` can also be changed at runtime with `/persona mode`.
## The Installed-page panel
In the Web GUI open **Plugins → Installed** and find `dsh-persona-slot`. Its `persona-slot` row is n
ow expandable: the arrow opens this plugin's own page, which owns:
- **Global persona (总人设)** — a multi-line editor; saving it applies to every session without its own

persona from the next model step.
- **Wildcard persona** — for sessions that have no persona of the

ir own.
- **Placement** — append after the deployment persona, replace it, or follow profile config.
- **Live sessions** — each live session's resolved persona, where it came from, and a Clear control
for sessions holding their own.
The panel refreshes every ten seconds and never overwrites text you have typed but not saved.
It talks to the plugin's own `/persona-slot/state` and `/persona-slot/update` routes instead of the
settings form, because that form's value field is single-line and cannot hold a character sheet. A p
anel save and a `/persona set` in a session write the same document, so the two never disagree.
## The `/persona` command
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Text is taken verbatim, multi-line included. A session id is only recognised after `for`, so `/perso
na set 你是猫娘` sets the persona to "你是猫娘" instead of treating it as a target.
## Where the runtime state lives
`$DSH_HOME/persona-slot/personas.json`
Profile configuration is a deployment default; this file is what the user typed. Keeping them apart
means a plugin upgrade, a profile rebuild, or a reinstall never erases a persona written in a sessio
n. A malformed file is moved aside as `personas.json.corrupt` and the plugin starts empty instead of
ormed file is moved aside as `personas.json.corrupt` and the plugin starts empty instead of failing.
### What the model sees
One additional prompt section (`append`) or a rewritten deployment persona (`replace`) holding the o
perator's persona text. The section is stable across steps until the persona changes, so provider pr
ompt caching keeps working between edits.
## Known limitations
- **Not a security boundary.** Personas are prompt text the operator writes. They do not restrict to

ols, sandbox mode, or approval policy — use those for enforcement.
- **The panel needs an HTTP surfa
ce.** The routes are registered on `ctx.webServer`, so a headless or TUI composition has only the `/

persona` command.
- **No persona-length ceiling.** A very long persona is sent on every request and

consumes context; that cost is the operator's to budget.
- **Session ids, not titles.** Overrides ke
y on the session id. A resumed or forked session keeps the id, so its persona follows it; a title ch

ange does not move a persona.
- **One persona per session.** Two personas cannot be layered on one s

ession; combine them into one text.
- **`replace` needs a deployment persona slot.** It rewrites `de
ployment:persona-prefix`. If a composition mounted `dsh-persona` inside a preset without that sectio
n, `replace` still inserts the section at the front of the assembled prompt, so the session is never
inserts the section at the front of the assembled prompt, so the session is never left without one.
